twoDistinctCauses.providerMessage: Schemas contains too many parameters with union types (20 parameters with type arrays or anyOf). This causes exponential compilation cost. Reduce the number of nullable or union-typed parameters (limit: 16 parameters with union types).
twoDistinctCauses.mechanism: JUSTIFICATION_SCHEMA_247 declares four nullable fields (unresolvedElement, alongsideControlConsidered, whyAlongsideControlInsufficient, dischargingControlRef) as type ['string','null']. The K6 union replicates the justification object across five role branches, so 4 x 5 = 20 union-typed parameters reach the provider against a documented limit of 16.
twoDistinctCauses.whyNotCaughtEarlier: the §246 offline probe exercised only ref, refKind and driverRole. It never included the justification object, so the nullable fields were never counted. A single nullable field transmits fine (1 < 16), which is why an isolated check would have passed.

twoDistinctCauses.providerMessage: The compiled grammar is too large, which would cause performance issues. Simplify your tool schemas or reduce the number of strict tools.
twoDistinctCauses.mechanism: grammar compilation happens only under strict tool schemas. The Expert wire schema is too large for the provider to compile into a constrained grammar.
twoDistinctCauses.significance: this is independent of §247 and was latent. §243 transmitted the same §239 schema successfully because it sent WITHOUT the strict flag — the omission §244 identified as a defect and §246/§247 repaired. Enabling strict enforcement is what surfaced the size limit.

conclusion: The frozen executable configuration — strict structured-output enforcement applied to the Expert wire schema — cannot be transmitted to the provider at all, for either contract version. The six confirmation cases therefore produced no driver-role evidence of any kind.
